credentials.service.bearer.step2: Create a token with only the permissions your flow needs.
credentials.service.bearer.step3: Copy it and paste it here. Many services show a token only once.
credentials.service.bearer.step4: Add the domain of the API, for example api.example.com.
credentials.service.bearer.summary: For APIs that ask for Authorization: Bearer and a token.
Paste the whole value the API expects, including a prefix such as Bearer if it asks for one.
credentials.service.header.field.headerN: The header the API expects, for example X-API-Key or Authorization.

credentials.service.header.name: API key in a header
credentials.service.header.protection: The list of domains stops a badly built flow from leaking your key to another site.
credentials.service.header.step1: Open the dashboard of the service you want to call and find its API keys.
credentials.service.header.step2: Check its documentation for the header it expects, for example X-API-Key, and type that name here.
credentials.service.header.step3: Create a key, copy it and paste it. The service may show it only once.
credentials.service.header.step4: Add the domain of the API, for example api.example.com. If the API signs in through its own page (OAuth), look for its own credential in the list instead.
credentials.service.header.summary: For any API that wants a key in a header, such as X-API-Key.
